focus: Integrate the newly republished 1785/1786 original scans, the previously indexed but now directly examined 1819 Benjamin Beverage manuscript, and census/settlement hypotheses without creating family-tree edges.

sources.label: 1785 petition and March 1786 resolve
sources.limits: No surviving individual land lot/title proof is established solely by names on the original petition.

sources.label: Benjamin Beverage, History of Vinalhaven, dated 20 December 1819
sources.repository: Maine Historical Society, William D. Williamson papers, Coll. 62; Maine Memory Network 20801
sources.access: Both manuscript page images and complete provided transcription visually inspected at institutional host; host restrictions apply
sources.limits: The letter's author and date are evidenced by the institutional item, but assigning him to a specific genealogical profile/parentage needs distinct corroboration.

sources.label: Thomas Beverege — 1790 Vinalhaven first-census household, 1908 federal reprint
sources.access: published transcription reviewed, original census schedule not visually inspected
sources.limits: Unnamed persons in the household cannot be inferred as sons, daughters, spouse, sibling or the 1785 petition's Matthew.

sources.label: Walter Goodwin Davis, Part of Hancock County, Maine, in 1800, NEHGR 105 (1951):204–213,276–291
sources.access: Modern 2025 historical research cites original census 'from whence emigrated' column. A Beverage-specific origin line has not been read.
sources.limits: General origins reported for other settler families do not establish any particular Beveridge family's previous residence.

sources.label: Putnam, 18 March 1786 original settler residence declarations, Maine State Archives Box 001
sources.access: Finding-aid-grade reference only; actual archive box and Beveridge-specific entries not yet inspected
sources.limits: Do not invent arrival dates or grant lots for Beveridges.

observations.title: First settlement year reported in an 1819 letter
observations.statement: In December 1819, Benjamin Beverage stated that Vinalhaven/Fox Islands was first settled in 1765.
observations.limits: A community founding date reported 54 years later, not proof of any named Beveridge arriving in 1765.

observations.title: Original settlers' petition names three Beveridges
observations.statement: James, Thomas and Matthew Beveridge are legible in the surviving 1785 list; Matthew has conflicting or layered annotations 'a minor' and possibly 'major'.
observations.limits: A community petition list does not independently show the three people's relationships or the age/legal capacity of Matthew.

observations.title: Massachusetts resolves a conditional island grant
observations.statement: The original March 1786 resolve reports 16,527 surveyed acres and 72 settlers before January 1, 1784; an 1889 printing differs at this number.
observations.limits: Survey acreage is not an individual Beveridge land allotment or a complete deed record.

observations.title: Thomas Beverege household counted in Vinalhaven
observations.statement: The later federal census transcription counts 2 free white males aged 16+, 4 younger males, 5 females, total 11.
observations.limits: Household co-residents and identity of the enumerated Thomas remain unverified from original schedule.

observations.title: Early unusual migration-origin column may identify earlier homes
observations.statement: The 1800 Vinalhaven return reportedly noted prior towns of emigration. No specific Beverage answer has been recovered or verified.
observations.limits: Never assign a town or colony of origin without the surname's exact original entry.

observations.title: Benjamin Beverage describes the islands in his own words
observations.statement: His two-page surviving letter addresses land titles, farming, schools, fishing, local religious life and names the author's preference not to be treated as an authority.
observations.limits: Contains historically valuable testimony and opinion but does not directly identify Benjamin's parents, children, or links to 1785 petitioners.

selected_facts.detail: The letter reports settlement beginning in 1765, incorporation in June 1789, and a name honoring Boston lawyer John Vinal that the inhabitants had not requested and allegedly disliked.
selected_facts.qualification: The name sentiment is Benjamin's reported local opinion, not a survey of inhabitants.

selected_facts.detail: The letter says the inhabitants held fee-simple title based on a Massachusetts grant, notes a general 1785 survey, and rounds the island area to roughly 17,000 acres.
selected_facts.qualification: Compare separately with the exact 16,527-acre figure given in the March 1786 resolve. Rounding is plausible but not proof the two measurements cover exactly identical parcels.

selected_facts.detail: Benjamin estimated land prices from one to twenty dollars per acre in 1819.
selected_facts.qualification: A period account of general values, not proof of any Beveridge family's transaction or lot.

selected_facts.detail: He reports approximately seven hundred tons of vessels, mostly fishing boats, plus three stores, three sawmills and two gristmills.
selected_facts.qualification: Contemporary descriptive count, not a government statistical return.

selected_facts.detail: He describes eight school districts, roughly three hundred scholars aged 4–16, and about $400 annually raised for schools.
selected_facts.qualification: The figures are Benjamin's own 1819 estimates.

selected_facts.detail: He describes Baptist and Methodist congregations, supported by voluntary subscriptions, and ends by asking that his name not be used as authority.
selected_facts.qualification: His stated authority caveat is important context for evaluating his historical recollections.

letter_analysis.image_reproduction: Do not mirror or rehost Maine Memory Network's image or PDF without rights permission; link directly to the institutional item and its complete hosted transcription.
